# Setup

```{r}
# Load packages
pacman::p_load(tidyverse, countrycode, knitr)
```

```{r}
# Load data frames
before2017 <- read.csv("original files/before2017_fixed_wo_traintest.csv")
master_US <- read.csv("original files/master_US_2021-2022.csv")
states2016 <- read.csv("original files/states2016.csv")
```

# Data exploration

How many before2017 texts are not seperated by blank spaces between words?

```{r}
str_count(before2017$texts, "[:blank:]")|>
  hist(breaks = 6000, xlim = c(0, 200))

str_count(master_US$texts, "[:blank:]")|>
  hist(breaks = 8000, xlim = c(0, 200))
```

```{r}
master_US |>
  mutate(count = str_count(texts, "[:blank:]")) |>
  filter(count == 0) |>
  kable()
```

All `before2017` texts contains at least some blank spaces, but there are 34 texts from `master_US` that does not have any spaces nor any texts.

Is the `cowc` column from the `countrycode` package the same `calph` in `states2016`?

```{r}
full_join(states2016 |>
            mutate(union = calph) |>
            select(calph, union),
          countrycode::codelist |>
            mutate(union = cowc) |>
            select(cowc, union),
          by = "union"
)|>
  arrange(calph, union)|>
  kable()
```

`codelist` have 20 more country codes than `states2016`

# Labeling texts

```{r}
# Create dictionary from `codelist` and `states2016`
codelist <- countrycode::codelist |> 
  select(cowc, country.name.en.regex) |>
  filter(cowc %in% states2016[-1,]$calph) |>  # `-1` excludes US
  
  # Add capitals
  left_join(states2016 |> 
              select(cowc = calph, capital, capital2, capital3), 
            by = "cowc") |>  
  
  # Turn to a named list
 mutate(regex_list = pmap(list(country.name.en.regex, capital, capital2, capital3), ~ discard(c(...), ~ is.na(.x) || .x == ""))) |>
  select(cowc, regex_list) |> 
  deframe()
```

```{r}
# Fixing codelist
# New ROK:
codelist[["ROK"]] <- c(
  "republic.*of.*korea(?!.*democratic)|\\bs.*korea|rok|r\\.o\\.k|(?!.*d.*p.*r)(?!.*democrat)(?!.*dem.*rep)(?!.*people)(?!.*north).*\\bkorea(?!.*d.*p.*r)(?!.*dem.*rep)",
  "Seoul"
)

# New PRK:
codelist[["PRK"]] <- c(
  "democratic.*peoples.*republic.*korea|north.*korea|dprk|d\\.p\\.r\\.k|korea.*peoples|peoples.*korea",
  "Pyongyang"
)
```

```{r}
# Labeling function
text_to_label <- function(sentence, country_list) {
  
  # Create a list with COW code as names and occurrence counts as values
  country_counts <- setNames(
    sapply(names(country_list), function(cowc) {
      sum(sapply(country_list[[cowc]], function(regex) str_count(sentence, regex(regex, ignore_case = TRUE))))
    }), 
    names(country_list)
  )
  
  # Remove countries with zero occurrences
  country_counts <- country_counts[country_counts > 0]
  
  # If no country is mentioned, return "0"
  if (length(country_counts) == 0) {
    return(0)
  }
  
  # Find countries with max counts
  top_countries <- names(country_counts[country_counts == max(country_counts)])
  
  # If there's a tie, return "0", otherwise return the most mentioned COWC code
  if (length(top_countries) > 1) {
    return(0)
  } else {
    return(top_countries)
  }
}
```

```{r}
text_to_label <- function(sentence, country_list) {
  # Pre-compile all regex patterns once
  compiled_patterns <- lapply(country_list, function(country_variants) {
    lapply(country_variants, function(pattern) {
      regex(pattern, ignore_case = TRUE)
    })
  })
  
  # Initialize counts vector with named zeros
  country_counts <- setNames(numeric(length(country_list)), names(country_list))
  
  # Count occurrences for each country
  for (cowc in names(country_list)) {
    # Sum up matches for all variants of this country
    total_matches <- 0
    for (pattern in compiled_patterns[[cowc]]) {
      matches <- str_count(sentence, pattern)
      if (matches > 0) {
        total_matches <- total_matches + matches
        if (total_matches > max(country_counts)) {
          # If this country already has more matches than others, it will win
          # unless there's a tie later
          break
        }
      }
    }
    if (total_matches > 0) {
      country_counts[cowc] <- total_matches
    }
  }
  
  # Find countries with maximum counts
  max_count <- max(country_counts)
  if (max_count == 0) {
    return(0)
  }
  
  # Get countries with max count
  top_countries <- names(country_counts[country_counts == max_count])
  
  # Return result based on whether there's a tie
  if (length(top_countries) > 1) {
    return(0)
  } else {
    return(top_countries)
  }
}
```

```{r}
labeled_before2017 <- before2017 |>
  mutate(COW = sapply(texts, text_to_label, country_list = codelist))
```

write.csv(labeled_before2017, file = "labeled_before2017.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```{r}
labeled_master_US <- master_US[1:100,]|>
  mutate(COW = sapply(texts, text_to_label, country_list = codelist))
```

```{r}
write.csv(labeled_master_US, file = "labeled_master_US1.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
labeled_master_US3 <- master_US[201:300,]|>
  mutate(COW = sapply(texts, text_to_label, country_list = codelist))
write.csv(labeled_master_US3, file = "labeled_master_US3.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```
